anatomy.flutter: ItemGroup(children) is a Column of rows with SizedBox gaps; Item(media, content, actions, variant, alignStart) is a Container > IntrinsicHeight > Row[media?, Expanded(content), actions?]; ItemMedia/ItemContent/ItemTitle/ItemDescription/ItemActions are the five companion slot widgets — matching the web's data-slot set minus ItemSeparator/ItemHeader/ItemFooter, explicitly recorded as not-ported.
anatomy.web: ItemGroup wraps each child in a <div role="listitem" data-slot="item-wrapper">; Item is a <div>/<Slot.Root> carrying itemVariants(); ItemMedia/ItemContent/ItemTitle/ItemDescription/ItemActions/ItemHeader/ItemFooter/ItemSeparator are exported — Flutter's own library doc explicitly records ItemSeparator, ItemHeader and ItemFooter as not ported ("no call site").

api.flutter: Item's variant is a 3-value ItemVariant enum (normal/outline/muted) and size does not exist as a parameter at all — no `size` argument on Item, ItemGroup, or any slot widget.
api.web: itemVariants declares both a `variant` axis (default/outline/muted) AND a `size` axis (default/sm/xs) with real class differences — `xs` uses gap-2 px-2.5 py-2 vs default's gap-2.5 px-3 py-2.5, and ItemMedia's image variant shrinks per group-data-[size=sm]/[size=xs], ItemContent's gap collapses at xs, and ItemDescription drops to text-xs at xs.
api.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: item.tsx's own library doc says size sm/xs were deliberately left unbuilt because 'their rungs are byte-identical to default for sm' and their only visible effect was believed to be the group's gap alone — but that is only true for the base Item classes. It is NOT true of ItemMedia's `image` variant (group-data-[size=sm]/item:size-8 group-data-[size=xs]/item:size-6, item.tsx:148), ItemContent's `group-data-[size=xs]/item:gap-0` (item.tsx:177), or ItemDescription's `group-data-[size=xs]/item:text-xs` (item.tsx:203) — none of which have a Flutter counterpart. A row that needs the xs/sm size axis (smaller media, tighter content gap, smaller description type) cannot express it in the Flutter Item at all, only ItemGroup's own gap can be tightened via gapOverride.

states.flutter: Item is a StatelessWidget with no interaction state of its own — no hover/focus/pressed handling anywhere in item.dart; the doc comment explicitly records `focus-visible:` as not ported because "a <div> takes no focus".
states.web: item.tsx's own doc comment records the same reasoning from the other direction: the hover surface ([a]:hover:bg-muted / [button]:hover:bg-muted) and focus-visible:border-ring / ring-3 / ring-ring/50 only apply when `asChild` renders a real <button> or <a>, which the ported base corpus never does — so no interaction state is reachable on either platform's plain-div Item.
states.note: n/a because a plain, non-asChild Item — the only shape either the Flutter or the base web corpus builds — is a static container with no focusable/hoverable/pressable state on either platform. asChild + a real <button>/<a> (which does carry these states on the web) is explicitly recorded as not ported to Flutter at all, which is really an anatomy/api gap (no asChild) rather than a states gap on the shape both platforms actually render.

disabled.flutter: Item has no `enabled`/`disabled` parameter anywhere in item.dart — there is no disabled path to explain or recover from.
disabled.web: Item likewise has no disabled prop or disabled: variant in itemVariants — a row is either shown or not shown; any disabled affordance lives on a child control (e.g. a disabled Button inside ItemActions) rather than on Item itself.
disabled.note: Neither platform gives Item a disabled concept — it is a passive container, so the dimension does not apply to either side; a disabled row is expressed by disabling the interactive child inside it, which is out of this component's scope on both platforms.

interaction.flutter: No keyboard/pointer/touch handling in item.dart — Item composes children but adds no GestureDetector, Focus, or MouseRegion of its own.
interaction.web: Item adds no onClick/onKeyDown of its own either; item.tsx's doc comment records that the agent console's "New chat" row had to re-add hover:bg-muted at its own call site precisely because Item furnishes no interaction behaviour when it is not asChild over a real control.
interaction.note: Interaction is deliberately out of scope for both platforms' Item — any pointer/keyboard handling belongs to whatever real control (a Button in ItemActions, or an asChild <button>/<a> the web supports but Flutter does not) lives inside or wraps the row.

semantics.flutter: ItemGroup builds a plain Column with no role/semantics wrapping at all — no Semantics(container:...) equivalent to role="list", and Item/ItemContent/etc. add no per-row role either.
semantics.web: ItemGroup renders role="list" on the group div AND, as of the fix documented in item.tsx's own comment block (lines 8-33), wraps every real child in <div role="listitem" data-slot="item-wrapper">, specifically because axe was reporting aria-required-children and a screen reader was announcing an EMPTY list at every ItemGroup call site before the fix landed.
semantics.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: This is the exact bug item.tsx's own comment describes fixing on the web ("role=\"list\" on the group was a claim with nothing behind it ... a screen reader read an EMPTY list wherever this component is used") — and Flutter's ItemGroup has never had any role/list semantics at all, so it reproduces neither the original bug's symptom (there is no role="list" claim to begin with) nor the fix (there is no listitem wrapping either). A screen reader on the Flutter side gets no list structure whatsoever around an ItemGroup, which is a real, currently-unaddressed gap relative to the web's fixed behaviour.
